description: First golden fixture for OCaml (#6812) — until this landed, NOTHING about internal/extractors/ocaml was graded. Three files carry the constructs the `inherit` question turns on: `inherit` inside `object ... end` at a class declaration (shapes.ml), `inherit` inside a class TYPE and the module-level `include`/`open` that look like it and are not it (containers.ml), and `inherit` inside an `object ... end` nested in a `let` BODY (render.ml) — the one context where the keyword is reachable by the CALLS scanner today, and therefore the only one this fixture can grade in both directions. HIERARCHY IS NOW GRADED, BY #6370's OCaml ARM. It was deliberately ungraded until then, in either direction, so that the arm would grade it rather than inherit someone else's expectations; six expected rows (four EXTENDS from `class ... object inherit`, one EXTENDS from a `class type`, one IMPLEMENTS from a `class : class-type` annotation) and nine new forbidden rows now do. Two pre-existing rows had to CHANGE DIALECT rather than merely gain siblings, because the arm introduces class entities and `printer` and `stream_writer` stopped being unresolvable strings; both are re-verified and the reason is written into each. Four class declarations were ADDED to containers.ml purely to give four fences a FROM endpoint — a fence with no anchor cannot fire, and every one of them is demonstrated firing under its own mutant. UNTIL #6370's OCaml ARM, OCaml emitted no EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS and this fixture asserted no hierarchy row in EITHER direction for the object/class-type forms, so as not to repeat the erlang-otp-mini trap of pinning a missing edge as correct; it forbade only the shapes that are NOT inheritance in any OCaml, a module `include` becoming a hierarchy edge, because those stay forbidden whatever the arm does. THE ARM HAS LANDED AND BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE NOW ASSERTED: six expected hierarchy rows and nine further fences, enumerated above. The `include` fences are unchanged and still fire. ONE PRINCIPLE GOVERNS EVERY ROW HERE, applied in both directions after a review found it applied in neither: a row is kept only if it has been DEMONSTRATED capable of firing, by a mutant, and dropped otherwise. That is why all FIFTEEN forbidden relationships and both forbidden entities carry a FIRES verdict with the mutant named — six from #6812 and nine from #6370's arm, each demonstrated by its own emission rather than by a sibling's, including the three future-facing hierarchy fences that were originally argued to be unfireable and were in fact merely mis-dialected; and it is why ten of nineteen subtype assertions were dropped as redundant while `make_logger`/`make_counter` keep theirs — those two are the `let x = object … end` pair a CST-backed producer could genuinely reclassify, so the assertion distinguishes something. “Aimed at a future producer” is a reason to write a row, never a reason to skip demonstrating that it works. Known divergences present in the source and deliberately NOT asserted, so nobody reads their absence as approval: the functor `module Make (C : Comparable) = struct` is not extracted at all (moduleRE requires `=`/`:` immediately after the name, and a parameter list intervenes); `method` and `val` produce no entity (`class` and `class type` DO, since #6370's arm — twelve of them are asserted above, and the sentence that used to stand here said they were all invisible); indented `let`s inside a module body are not extracted, which also means module CONTAINS is empty here; and every module in containers.ml reports the SAME end line, which is the depth-walker defect measured in the PR that added this fixture.

expected_entities.name: point
expected_entities.note: Top-level record type. Baseline non-object extraction in the file that holds the object cases, so a regression that killed shapes.ml wholesale is distinguishable from one that only touched objects.

expected_entities.name: bounds
expected_entities.note: SECOND type in the same file: typeRE de-duplicates by name, and a fixture with one type per file cannot tell 'types work' from 'the first type works'.

expected_entities.name: level
expected_entities.note: A variant type rather than a record — the type-declaration RHS varies while the position (column 0) is held constant.

expected_entities.name: shapes.ml
expected_entities.note: The file entity is the carrier of the IMPORTS edge for `open Printf` — OCaml anchors imports on the file, not on a module entity, so without this row the import assertions below have no from endpoint to name.

expected_entities.name: Comparable
expected_entities.note: `module type Comparable = sig ... end` — the `module type` arm of moduleRE, and the only entity here whose body is a `sig` rather than a `struct`.

expected_entities.name: Base
expected_entities.note: A plain `module ... = struct`. Target of the `include` in Extended.

expected_entities.name: Extended
expected_entities.note: The module that `include`s another. It must exist as a module and must NOT gain a hierarchy edge — see forbidden_relationships.

expected_entities.name: render_with
expected_entities.note: Declared AFTER two `class type ... object ... end` blocks. A let-extractor whose column-0 anchor were loosened, or whose scan were confused by the intervening `object`/`end` keywords, loses this one first.

expected_entities.name: make_logger
expected_entities.note: #6812 CENTRAL ROW: a `let` whose body IS an `object ... end` containing `inherit`. This is the only context in the fixture where the `inherit` line is inside a scanned body, and therefore the only one where over-firing on the keyword is observable.

expected_entities.name: make_counter
expected_entities.note: #6812 NEGATIVE CONTROL for the row above: the same `let x = object ... end` shape with NO `inherit`. Holds the object nesting constant and varies only the presence of the keyword.

expected_entities.name: append_all
expected_entities.note: #6812 identifier hazard, the NON-triggering half: `end` here is followed by `_`, and Go treats `_` as a word character, so `\bend\b` re-run against the remaining slice does NOT match inside `end_all`. Paired with `backend` and `legend` below, which do end at a word boundary and do match. Stated this precisely because an earlier version spelled all three with a trailing `_word`, so the axis it claimed to vary contained only this case. NOT GRADED by an assertion: nothing in this fixture asserts a module span, and the hazard only reaches extractModuleBody, so these three put both outcomes in the corpus rather than fencing either.

expected_entities.name: backend
expected_entities.note: #6812 identifier hazard, the TRIGGERING half: `backend` ends at a word boundary, so the slice-relative `\bend\b` matches and the scanner reads a closing keyword inside an identifier. Also the target of a forbidden CALLS row, which is what makes the name itself load-bearing rather than decorative.

expected_entities.name: legend
expected_entities.note: #6812 identifier hazard, triggering, second spelling: `legend` differs from `backend` in everything but the trailing `end`, so a fix keyed on one word does not pass by accident. Two triggering names and one non-triggering name is the whole axis.

expected_entities.name: shape
expected_entities.note: #6370: the class vocabulary this arm had to introduce — #6939 (2) records that NO `class` construct produced any entity before it, and a hierarchy edge has no FROM node without one. `shape` is the root of the file's chain and is declared `class virtual`, so the `virtual` token sitting between the keyword and the name is held as a varied axis against the plain `class circle` below.

expected_entities.name: circle
expected_entities.note: #6370: a class that is BOTH a child (of shape) and a parent (of tagged_circle). The only entity in the fixture on both ends of an EXTENDS edge, so a producer that emits leaves-only or roots-only is distinguishable.

expected_entities.name: square
expected_entities.note: #6370: the `inherit shape "square" as super` form. Holds the parent constant against `circle` and varies only the `as super` binding, which a target reader could mistake for a second parent.

expected_entities.name: labelled
expected_entities.note: #6370: `class virtual labelled` with NO `inherit` at all — the negative control for the entity axis. A class must become an entity whether or not it has a parent, which is what keeps entity extraction separable from edge extraction.

expected_entities.name: tagged_circle
expected_entities.note: #6370: the MULTIPLE-inheritance case, two `inherit` clauses in one object body.

expected_entities.name: printer
expected_entities.note: #6370: `class type printer = object ... end` → subtype class_type, not class and not interface. It is the target of both the EXTENDS from verbose_printer and the IMPLEMENTS from basic_printer, so one entity carries both hierarchy kinds on its inbound side.

expected_entities.name: verbose_printer
expected_entities.note: #6370: a class TYPE that inherits another class type. The clause is a different grammar node (inheritance_specification under class_body_type) from the class form's inheritance_definition under object_expression, so the two arms are graded separately.

expected_entities.name: basic_printer
expected_entities.note: #6370: `class basic_printer : printer = object ... end` — a CLASS (not a class type) whose class-type annotation is the fixture's only IMPLEMENTS source.

expected_entities.name: relay_printer
expected_entities.note: #6370: exists to give the module-qualified-parent fence a FROM endpoint. Its `inherit Remote.printer` must produce NO edge; without the entity the forbidden row below would have nothing to anchor on and could never fire.

expected_entities.name: remote_relay
expected_entities.note: #6370: exists to give the unresolved-target fence a FROM endpoint. `inherit external_base` names a class declared nowhere in this file. Held separate from relay_printer because the two are rejected by DIFFERENT guards and a single case would grade only whichever ran first.

expected_entities.name: spawning_printer
expected_entities.note: #6370: exists to give the nested-object fence a FROM endpoint. Its `inherit` sits in an object nested inside a METHOD, which belongs to that object and not to this class.

expected_entities.name: stream_writer
expected_entities.note: #6370: the class `make_logger`'s anonymous object inherits. It is a real class binding and so becomes an entity; the anonymous object that inherits it is NOT, which is why the pair produces a CALLS edge and no hierarchy edge.

expected_relationships.note: #6812 THE ROW THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR, RE-DIALECTED BY #6370's OCaml arm. `inherit stream_writer prefix` sits inside make_logger's ANONYMOUS object body: there is no class binding to anchor a hierarchy edge on, so the parent name still survives only as a CALLS edge from the enclosing function, exactly as #6812 measured. What changed is the TO side. `stream_writer` is now an extracted class entity, so the CALLS target RESOLVES to it and its ToID is a content hash rather than the literal string; to_bare_name can no longer match and the row was rewritten to to_name + to_kind + to_file. This is the trap the arm was warned about and is recorded rather than absorbed: the row is STRONGER now (it asserts the edge binds to the right node, not merely that a string survived), and leaving it in the bare dialect would have made it fail rather than silently pass. Paired with the forbidden make_logger --[EXTENDS]--> stream_writer row: the name must reach the graph as a call and NOT as a hierarchy edge attributed to the enclosing `let`.

The only row in the fixture whose TO side resolves to a real entity rather than a bare name, so a regression that stopped binding CALLS targets to entities is distinguishable from one that stopped emitting CALLS at all.

The module-qualified call form (callDotRE) rather than the bare form. Emitted from the body of the function whose NAME contains the substring the block scanner treats as a closing keyword — if that hazard ever truncates the body, this row goes first.

#6812: `open Printf` is an IMPORT. The whole question this fixture serves is whether the module-composition keywords stay distinct from inheritance, and this is the row that pins the one of them that IS an edge today.

#6812: `open List` in the same file as `include Base`. Paired with the forbidden `Extended -> Base` rows: `open` produces an edge, `include` must not produce a hierarchy one. A fixture carrying only one of the two keywords cannot tell a producer that handles both apart from one that handles neither.

A member of the object make_counter returns. Held as an EXPECTED row here and as a FORBIDDEN row from make_logger: the same identifier must be reachable from its own function and unreachable from the previous one, which is what makes the let-body boundary graded in both directions rather than one.

#6370 THE ROW THE ARM EXISTS FOR: `class circle radius = object inherit shape "circle" ... end`. Before it, OCaml emitted no EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS by any of the three producer paths — its own extractor, cross/hierarchy's supportedLanguages, and the YAML rule packs under internal/engine/rules/ (all three checked). The parent is carried by a class_application node because the clause passes an argument, which is a different carrier from the bare class_path in tagged_circle's second parent below.
#6370: the same parent through the `as super` form. Two children of one parent, so a producer that keys a parent to at most one child is distinguishable from one that does not.
#6370: multiple inheritance, FIRST clause — and the only edge in the fixture whose TARGET is itself a child, so a producer that walks a chain one level deep is distinguishable.

#6370: multiple inheritance, SECOND clause. A producer that takes only the first `inherit` in a body passes the row above and fails this one; the pair is what makes 'all clauses' graded rather than 'a clause'. Carried by a bare class_path (no arguments), against the class_application above.

#6370: the class-TYPE arm. `class type verbose_printer = object inherit printer ... end` reaches the producer through inheritance_specification / class_type_path, an entirely different pair of node types from the class form. This row is what distinguishes an arm that handles class types from one that handles only classes — and it sits in the file whose `include`, `open` and functor are all forbidden from minting the same edge.

#6370: the only IMPLEMENTS the arm emits. `class basic_printer : printer = object ... end` constrains the class to a class type, which is OCaml's interface-conformance shape. Written as a separate KIND rather than as a second EXTENDS because #6370's audit found languages sitting on both sides of that confusion; paired with the forbidden basic_printer --[EXTENDS]--> printer row so the choice is graded in both directions.

forbidden_relationships.note: #6812 OVER-FIRING, the keyword itself: `inherit` sits in ocamlKeywords (extractor.go:99) as one of ~60 CALLS-blocklist entries. FIRES, verified: deleting the `"inherit": true` entry produces exactly this edge, because callBareRE matches `inherit ` in make_logger's object body. This is the row that makes the keyword suppression graded rather than incidental — before this fixture, removing that entry broke nothing.

#6812 OVER-FIRING, body boundary: `bump` is a method of the NEXT function's object (make_counter), one top-level declaration further down. FIRES, verified: deleting the `break` in extractLetBody (extractor.go:401) makes make_logger's body run to end-of-file and produces this edge. Paired with the expected `make_counter -> bump` row, so a producer that over-reaches is distinguishable from one that under-reaches.

#6812 OVER-FIRING, body boundary, second hop: `backend` is TWO top-level declarations past make_logger. FIRES under the same mutant as the row above, and is stated with a RESOLVED to side rather than a bare one on purpose — `bump` is a method name that binds to nothing, `backend` is a top-level function that binds to an entity, so the two rows also grade the forbidden matcher on both of its target dialects. A single row written the other way round would have been silently unfireable: to_bare_name only matches an edge whose target stayed a raw string, which this one does not.

#6812 OVER-FIRING, `include` is not inheritance: `include Base` splices a module's contents into Extended. It is module composition, not a class-inheritance edge, and it stays forbidden after #6370's OCaml arm lands — which is why this row is safe to write while the object-form hierarchy edge is deliberately left ungraded. FIRES, verified: a mutant emitting Extended --[EXTENDS]--> Base from the `include` produces exactly this hit. Written with to_bare_name first, it was SILENTLY UNFIREABLE — Base is a top-level module that binds to an entity, so an edge to it carries a RESOLVED target and to_bare_name can never match it; the mutant emitted the edge and the fence reported zero. The reason then given for the non-firing, that OCaml has no hierarchy vocabulary to mutate, was an argument rather than a demonstration, and it was wrong: the cause was the target dialect, and on the day #6370's arm emits this edge both fences would have passed.

#6812 OVER-FIRING: the same claim in the other hierarchy kind. Written separately because a producer that emits IMPLEMENTS where it means EXTENDS passes a fence naming only one of them — the exact confusion the #6370 audit found languages sitting on either side of. FIRES, verified with its OWN mutant emitting IMPLEMENTS rather than EXTENDS, because a fence verified only through its sibling is a fence verified once.

#6812 OVER-FIRING, cross-construct, RE-DIALECTED BY #6370's OCaml arm. `class type verbose_printer = object inherit printer ... end` sits in the same file as `module type Comparable = sig ... end`. A producer that finds `inherit` by searching a file rather than by anchoring inside a class binding attributes it to whichever `module`/`class` declaration it last saw, and moduleRE's last match in this file is Comparable. The row previously used to_bare_name on the stated ground that `printer` is a class type and produces no entity at all. #6370's arm makes that false — `printer` is now a SCOPE.Component subtype class_type — so the fence would have become SILENTLY UNFIREABLE in exactly the way its own note warned about, and it is rewritten to the resolved dialect. FIRES, re-verified after the change with a mutant emitting Comparable --[EXTENDS]--> printer.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, module-qualified parent: `inherit Remote.printer` names a class in another module. Its LAST SEGMENT is `printer`, which is the name of a class type declared in this very file, so a producer that reduces a path to its final identifier binds the edge to the local node — an edge that exists, resolves, and points at the wrong thing, which is #6369's standing example. FIRES, verified: removing the module_path/extended_module_path rejection in pathLeafName produces exactly this hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, unresolved target: `inherit external_base` names a class declared nowhere in this file. analytics/scan.go keys touched[from] unconditionally, so emitting this DANGLING edge would improve the orphan rate exactly as much as a real one — the metric cannot tell them apart and only the producer can. FIRES, verified: removing the `declared[target]` gate in classEntities produces exactly this hit. THE to_bare_name IS THE PRODUCER'S OWN Format A STRUCTURAL REF, SPELLED OUT, AND THAT IS NOT A WORKAROUND — it is the only string such an edge can carry, because a target with no entity never resolves and this producer never writes a bare name. Writing `external_base` here instead would be a fence that cannot fire, which is the defect this fixture's governing principle exists to stop. It is also NOT the only instrument grading this guard: TestOCamlHierarchy_UndeclaredParentYieldsNoEdge_6370 kills the same mutant without naming a spelling at all, so a future change to the ToID dialect breaks this row loudly rather than disarming the guard silently. Held SEPARATE from relay_printer because that case is rejected by the qualified-path guard and this one by the resolution gate, and with only one of the two inputs present the two guards would mask each other and neither would be graded.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, attribution depth: `method spawn = object inherit basic_printer end` — the `inherit` belongs to the object the method returns, not to the class that declares the method. This is the same defect class #6812 measured on the depth walker (230 of 408 attributions wrong), reappearing as a tree walk that descends instead of reading direct children. FIRES, verified: making inheritEdges search descendants instead of the binding's own object body produces exactly this hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, wrong KIND, class form: `inherit` is class inheritance and must be EXTENDS. A producer that emits IMPLEMENTS instead passes every recall row that names only a kind it does emit. FIRES, verified: swapping the kind literal in inheritEdges produces exactly this hit.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, wrong KIND, class-TYPE form. Written separately from the row above because the two arms build their edges from different node types and a single kind literal shared between them is an assumption, not a fact. FIRES, verified with its own mutant, because a fence verified through its sibling is a fence verified once.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, wrong KIND, the other direction: the `: printer` annotation is conformance, not inheritance, and must be IMPLEMENTS. Paired with the expected basic_printer --[IMPLEMENTS]--> printer row, so a producer that collapses both hierarchy kinds into one is caught whichever kind it collapses onto. FIRES, verified with a mutant emitting EXTENDS from the class-type annotation.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, `open` is not inheritance: `open List` is an import and already carries an IMPORTS row in this fixture. The pairing is the point — the same keyword must produce an edge of one kind and never one of the other. to_bare_name and deliberately: List is an import placeholder that is pruned and never becomes a resolvable entity, which is the same dialect its expected IMPORTS row uses. FIRES, verified with a mutant emitting containers.ml --[EXTENDS]--> List.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, functor application is not inheritance: `module Make (C : Comparable) = struct ... end` is OCaml's generics, and `C : Comparable` looks exactly like a conformance annotation. The FROM side is the FILE and not `Make` because `Make` is extracted as no entity at all (#6939 (1), deliberately unfixed here), so a file-anchored producer is the only shape this fence can be written against — which also makes it a fence against the #6295/#6298 file-anchoring defect. FIRES, verified with a mutant emitting containers.ml --[EXTENDS]--> Comparable.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, anonymous object: `let make_logger prefix = object inherit stream_writer prefix ... end` has no class binding, so there is no class for a hierarchy edge to anchor on. Attributing it to the enclosing `let` would produce a SCOPE.Operation that EXTENDS a class — a shape the graph has no reading for. The name still reaches the graph, as the CALLS edge asserted above, so this row and that one together say WHICH edge the construct is allowed to produce. FIRES, verified with a mutant emitting make_logger --[EXTENDS]--> stream_writer.

forbidden_entities.name: inherit
forbidden_entities.note: #6812: the keyword must never be promoted to an entity of its own. FIRES, verified: a mutant appending a SCOPE.Operation named `inherit` to extractOCaml's output produces exactly one forbidden entity hit, exit 2. Its earlier note claimed it was unreachable because nothing in extractOCaml creates an entity from a CALLS target — true of today's code and irrelevant to whether the ROW works, which is the only thing a fence's note should assert. Aimed at a grammar-backed producer, where an `inherit` CST node IS a node and naming it directly is the obvious slip.

forbidden_entities.name: object
forbidden_entities.note: #6812: `object` opens a block and is not a type. FIRES, verified with its own mutant appending a SCOPE.Component named `object`, scored separately from the row above because two fences verified by one mutant are one verification. Aimed at the producer that replaces this extractor.
